column1: # Known gaps: our open bugs, each one with a todo behind it.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a gap of ours -- a call plain Metal answers and we refuse, or a field that
# differs with nothing announced to justify it -- which, by the owner's standing rule that what
# Metal allows we must allow, is a bug of ours, written down so the one case that holds it visible
# does not make every run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. An accepted difference
# lives in `docs/API.md` section 10 and is justified; a degradation lives in the degrade catalogue
# and is announced. This file is neither. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# It is an EXPECTATION, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and `conformance replay` holds it to that in both
#   - a refusal or a divergence that is not listed here fails the run: a new gap appeared;
#   - a row listed here that the run no longer holds ALSO fails the run, saying the gap looks
#     fixed and the row must go.
# That second direction is the whole point. Closing a gap forces the ledger edit, so a row cannot
# outlive the bug it stands for and this file cannot rot into a silencer. It also means a row is
# checked by execution rather than by discipline, which is the standard the rest of the suite is
# held to. It has already earned its keep twice in this round: a product fix landed and the replay
# named four stale rows before anyone reasoned about the fix.
# The ledger changes the exit status and nothing else. The report still prints each of these as a
# `Refused` or `Divergent` row, with our answer and Metal's, with Metal's own words where its API
# validation refuses the call too, and counted in the suite's own numbers. Nothing is laundered.
# A row is held only against the cases a run selected and the venues it ran on, so replaying one
# case does not read every other row as fixed, and a run on one venue does not read another
# Tab-separated, SIX fields. Blank lines and lines from `#` are ignored.
#   venue       `*` for every venue, or words held (without case, as a substring) against the
#               venue's own description: its device name, driver, API version and Metal level.
#               `*` is the STRONGER claim, not the looser one -- the second direction then holds
#               the row on every venue the run selected the case on -- so widening a row's scope
#               makes it harder to satisfy, which is what stops a venue-scoped row from becoming a
#               way to silence a venue. A pattern that matches nothing holds the row nowhere, so
#               its gap reads as unlisted and the run fails: a typo is loud.
#   expects     `refused`, a call plain Metal answered and we did not; or `divergent`, a field that
#               differs with nothing announced to justify it. Nothing else is ever written down:
#               an unrecorded case and a stale recording must fail loudly, and a venue that
#               honestly lacks a feature is not a gap of ours at all.
#   site        the site, as node names from the root, exactly as the report prints it.
#   answer      what the run answers there, exactly as the report prints it after the site, which
#               `conformance replay` also emits as a ready-to-paste row so nobody has to
#               reconstruct it. For a refusal that is our typed error. For a divergence it is how
#               much moved: how many of the site's leaves differ and the largest difference where
#               the values are numbers. NOT the first mismatch -- a bound read off the first
#               mismatch is not a bound (four rotated-target rows differ by one code at their
#               first mismatch and reach two well past it), and a walk position is a property of
#               the data rather than of the bug, so it would rename the row whenever an earlier
#               leaf moved. The report prints that position on the line below, where it helps a
#               reader and binds nothing. Part of the row's identity, so a gap that changed into
#               another gap at the same site is a new gap and not this one.
#   waiting on  the open bug, in words: what Metal does, what we do instead, and where the fix
#               belongs. Not matched -- it is what a reader needs -- but a row must carry one.
# A row whose case is not in the tree yet cannot be committed: a test holds every live row to a
# case that exists AND to a site that case's committed recording actually holds, so a row for a
# site the case never produces is impossible rather than silently unheld. Leave such a row here as
# a `#` comment for the stream that owns the case; nothing is waiting today.

column5: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: MeshShading, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column6: The runtime refuses `drawMeshThreads` where the threads leave a partial object threadgroup, `Unsupported(MeshShading, NotImplemented)` out of the bind state (crates/metal2vulkan/src/bind/graphics.rs, `mesh_draw`'s `threads[i].is_multiple_of(lo[i])` test), while Metal draws it and runs the threads left over. Not a device gap: this M3 Max has mesh shading and draws every other row of the same probe. Measured on it (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, our probe gaps/mesh/obj, one shape per process): the draw launches ceil(threads/L) object threadgroups, `threads_per_grid` is the threads asked for, and the last threadgroup on an axis runs with the threads left over as a non-uniform threadgroup exactly as `dispatchThreads:` does for compute - `threads_per_threadgroup` is min(L, threads - group*L) per axis (6 of 64 reports 6), `thread_position_in_threadgroup` and `thread_index_in_threadgroup` run over that reduced size, `simdgroups_per_threadgroup` is ceil of it over 32, and a threadgroup barrier synchronizes the threads left over alone. The cause is that Vulkan has no partial workgroup: the exact form is the one compute already uses, a region per edge dispatched at its own local size, which for a draw means several draws of several pipeline specializations and, on a grid with more than one whole threadgroup on a higher axis, a primitive order that is not Metal's; the alternative is one draw of ceil groups with the object entry reading its reduced size from its `DispatchRegion` record (`MultiRegion` 1 already carries the grid and L, and already reports ceil threadgroups and the asked-for threads), deriving the thread position and index from `lin` over that size and returning before the body past it, which is exact for everything but a threadgroup barrier and so needs a pipeline variant whose compile refuses an object function that synchronizes. Neither is built. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Metal counts the quads the discard drops whole in a simdgroup sum that sits ahead of the discard for a measured reason -- the discard's condition reads the sum (`counted_dependent`), or a device store (`counted_store`) or an atomic (`counted_atomic`) lies between them -- so each kept texel's first channel, `before > after`, is 1. On the gate container's arm64 lavapipe (`llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 128 bits)`, the venue this row names) all four texels of the kept quad read 0, uniformly and each by exactly one code: our run's sum saw the same lane count before and after the discard. MoltenVK on this M3 Max answers Metal's 1 exactly, with no notice, so this is one venue's difference and not the module's rule being wrong (verified: a whole-set replay on each venue, 2026-10-23). The suite's other lavapipe, `llvmpipe (LLVM 23.1.1, 256 bits)` on x86-64, does not hold it and carries no row for this case, which is why the venue field names the 128-bit build rather than the bare substring `llvmpipe` that covers both: a row scoped to both read as stale on a venue the gap was never measured on. Two llvmpipe builds that differ in vector width and in LLVM release answering differently makes this the build's and not the module's, and it still does not say which of the two candidates below it is. The cause is NOT established, and the case as written cannot establish it: the four numbers it records per texel are identical under both candidates -- the device's fragment simdgroup holding only the kept quad, so the dropped quads were never in it (the target is 8 by 4, exactly one 32-lane simdgroup if the device packs it that way), and the device's compiler moving the reduction past the discard although `canon/discard_sink.rs` placed it ahead on purpose. Both give before == after and so (0, 0, 0, 0), on every texel alike, which is why the uniformity across the quad separates nothing either. The next step is the case's: record the simdgroup's own size and the raw `before` and `after` beside the four derived numbers, which separates the two at no cost, then fix whichever it is -- a device whose reduction does not see the dropped lanes needs the active set computed in the module rather than taken from the device's implicit one (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/simd/group.rs with crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/discard_sink.rs), and a device whose fragment simdgroup is smaller than Metal's is a different answer again. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, handed to whoever takes the discard-hoist family.

Metal's `tailSizeInBytes` exceeds our sparse model's on extreme aspect ratios: a 2D texture whose shorter axis is a handful of texels while the longer is a thousand or more. Each row's own two numbers are in its answer field. Measured, and sharper than it was: EVERY one of the 13 differences is a whole multiple of the 16384-byte page -- eleven of them one page, two of them (RGBA32Float, levels-4, 1000x3 and 3x1000) two pages -- and the answers are symmetric in the axes, so 1000x3 and 3x1000 give identical numbers for every format. The page count differs per format, and the rule that produces it is still unidentified; what is now established is that our model is short by whole pages rather than by a rounding, which rules out an alignment or ceiling error inside a page. The rows are scoped to every venue because the answer is CPU arithmetic over a descriptor in `crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture/heap_tiled.rs`, the same model on every device at one Metal level: verified identical, site for site and number for number, on MoltenVK on this M3 Max and on llvmpipe in the Linux container (2026-10-23), which is why `*` and not a venue. We believe Metal's answer and our model must both be re-derived before a fix: the model was fitted to ordinary shapes and these are outside what it was fitted to. No tolerance is right here -- the number is a byte count Metal states exactly, and a consumer sizing a heap from it would under-allocate. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list for the sparse stream.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: Some(RenderPipeline at Color(0)), symbol: None }"))
column6: Plain Metal on this M3 Max makes and runs a render pipeline whose ARGB8Unorm colour attachment blends with DestinationAlpha and OneMinusDestinationAlpha in the COLOUR factors, and stores every texel as the RGBA8Unorm leg's bytes rotated (recorded here over 3 runs, 8,192 texels, zero mismatches; Metal's own API validation let it run). The runtime refuses the pipeline Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented) at colour attachment 0, so the refusal is of something plain Metal does. The cause is structural rather than a policy: the runtime holds ARGB8Unorm in an R8G8B8A8_UNORM image of the rotated bytes, so the image's alpha channel carries Metal's BLUE and a colour factor that must read Metal's destination alpha would have to read the image's red. Vulkan has no such blend factor. The alpha-factor direction is already solved -- a second pipeline output of copies of Metal's source alpha (pipeline::rotated_blend) -- but that trick does not reach a DESTINATION channel, which only the framebuffer holds. The exact forms are a pass that keeps the rotated image's channels in Metal's order behind a swizzled view, or reading the destination in the fragment where the device offers programmable blending. Neither is built. Fix belongs in metal2vulkan's pipeline (rotated_blend) and the runtime's ARGB8Unorm image layout. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Metal's `MTLComputePipelineDescriptor.reset` is PARTIAL. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434), from `compute-descriptor-reset`'s own committed recording over three runs: the reset restores the label to nil, every `buffers[i].mutability` to `MTLMutabilityDefault`, `supportIndirectCommandBuffers` and `supportAddingBinaryFunctions` to false and `maxCallStackDepth` to 1, and leaves its three thread-shape properties exactly as the program set them -- `threadGroupSizeIsMultipleOfThreadExecutionWidth` true, `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` 96, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` 8 by 6 by 2. The runtime has no descriptor object, so the coverage map's counterpart for `reset` is `ComputePipelineDescriptor::new` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/descriptor.rs), a fresh value that resets all nine, and our side answers 0, 0 and false where Metal answers what was set. Nothing is announced for it, so by the standing rule it is a gap of ours. It is also very likely an Apple defect rather than a contract: in the same round `MTLTileRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores the analogous `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` and `threadgroupSizeMatchesTileSize` correctly (`tile-descriptor-reset` is exact) and `MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores every field it has (`mesh-descriptor-reset` is exact), so only the compute descriptor keeps anything. The fix is a choice between two forms and neither may be guessed at: a `ComputePipelineDescriptor::reset` that mirrors Metal's three kept fields, or an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10 saying a reset compute descriptor keeps its thread shape on Metal and not here. Mirroring an Apple bug in a published crate's API is the owner's call, so this is on the orchestrator's todo list rather than fixed here. Not a device gap: no venue is involved -- the difference is Metal's recorded answer against a plain Rust struct, so the row is every venue's.

`BinaryArchive` has three of Metal's four pipeline adders: `addMeshRenderPipelineFunctionsWithDescriptor:error:` has no counterpart at all. Metal takes the call, takes it a second time with the same descriptor, and then serialises the archive to a file that exists and holds bytes (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, from this case's own committed recording over three runs, plain Metal and under its API validation, which let the case run). Ours cannot be asked: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/mod.rs declares `add_compute_pipeline_functions` (:138), `add_render_pipeline_functions` (:161) and `add_tile_render_pipeline_functions` (:194) and no mesh form, and the module's own documentation lists the three as if they were all of them. The pieces for the fourth are already there: `metal2vulkan::pipeline::MeshPipelineDescriptor` exists and the runtime creates mesh states from it (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/render.rs:629), and the add's own shape is the render one -- create the state with `Some(&used)`, then keep what it used under the descriptor's archive keys -- so what is missing is the key function beside `metal_key::render` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/metal_key.rs:185) for an object-plus-mesh-plus-fragment triple, and the `check` arm that refuses a mesh creation on a miss (`binary_archive::check` is already called for the mesh path at crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/render.rs:1579, where the comment says outright that no archive holds a mesh render pipeline). It is deliberately NOT done here: adding `BinaryArchive::add_mesh_render_pipeline_functions` adds an item to a published crate's public surface and a new archive key form to its container, which needs docs/REFUSALS.md regenerated and the `api_surface` table updated, and this stream took no evidence for either. Every venue's: the gap is in the runtime's own API, before any Vulkan call. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's archive surface.

Metal accepts a **metallib** as a binary archive and we refuse it. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording over three runs: `newBinaryArchiveWithDescriptor:error:` with the descriptor's `url` set to a metallib of the case's own shader answers an archive, where the same call over a text file, an empty file, a missing path and a directory each answers `MTLBinaryArchiveDomain` code 1 (the four rows this case compares beside it, all four of which we match exactly). What Metal does with such an archive is not measured here -- whether it holds anything, or is simply an empty archive that happens to have read a container it recognises -- and that is the first thing the fix needs. Ours refuses at `container::read` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/container.rs:183), which reads the file whole and hands it to `decode`, whose first act is to check the suite-private magic `M2VBARCH` and a version word (container.rs:116, the magic at :37); a metallib starts `MTLB`, so `decode` answers `None` and the creation becomes `BinaryArchive(InvalidFile)` (container.rs:240). By the owner's standing rule that what Metal allows we must allow, the refusal is the bug. The fix is to decide what a non-archive container means and say so: either accept a file that parses as a metallib as an archive that holds no entry (which is what Metal's answer is consistent with, and which `Library::from_metallib` can already tell), or keep refusing and record an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10. The first changes a published crate's documented refusal surface -- `Device::new_binary_archive`'s own doc comment states that a file that is missing or not an archive is `BinaryArchive(InvalidFile)` 'as Metal answers for a missing, empty, garbage or text file and for a directory', a list measured on an M3 Max and an M4 that is correct as far as it goes and simply never asked about a metallib -- so it is not this stream's call. Every venue's: the refusal is in the container reader, before any Vulkan call. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's archive surface.

Metal's `MTLAttributeStrideStatic` on a `[[stage_in]]` layout of `MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic` is not "read at stride 0"; it fetches the element at the bind offset for the FIRST element and hands every element past it ZERO. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from these cases' own committed recordings: a dynamic layout over a buffer holding `0x10 + e` at element `e`, eight threads stepping by thread position in x at rate 1, bound with the constant, answered `0x110` and then `0x100` seven times (the fixture writes the attribute plus `0x100`), while a bind at stride 0 answered `0x110` eight times -- so the two are different answers and Metal's validation stops neither. The same shape at a bind offset of 8 answered `0x112` and then `0x100` seven times, which says the bind offset still reaches the first element. Ours answers the stride-0 reading: `attribute_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/argument_table.rs:377) maps the constant to `None`, `None` removes the index's entry from `ArgumentTable::attribute_strides`, and every reader of that map takes a missing entry as 0 -- the binder's push constant `PushField::StageInStride` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs:179, whose own module note at line 28 says "as 0 for a buffer bound without one") and the reach check (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/fetch_reach.rs:112). So the fetch walks elements at stride 0 and every thread reads element 0, which is a silently wrong answer rather than a refusal. The runtime already knows the real behaviour for ONE of the four setters: `ComputeCommandEncoder::set_bytes_with_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/compute.rs:607) documents "an M4 read element 0 of the bytes and zeros past it" and refuses that combination `NotImplemented(KernelStageIn)` rather than emulating it -- this oracle shows the buffer forms behave the same way, so the note on the buffer forms (argument_table.rs:377 and compute.rs:509, "one bound without a stride reads at stride 0") is what is wrong, not the inline-bytes one. The fix belongs in the fetch, not in the table: `PushField::StageInStride` needs to be able to say "the constant was bound" apart from "stride 0" -- a sentinel value or a flag beside it -- and the pulled read in crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs must then select the element at the bind offset where the element index is 0 and a zero of the attribute's form otherwise, which is the same predicate the inline-bytes form would need and would let that refusal be dropped too. It is deliberately NOT done here: this stream's target is the conformance suite, the change is to a published crate's shader lowering and its push-constant ABI (so it moves `SEMANTICS_VERSION` and every stage-in recording), and it needs release-mode evidence this stream has not taken. Scoped to every venue because the gap is in the push constant and the fetch's own arithmetic, before any device behaviour -- measured on this M3 Max alone, so every other venue is expected and unaudited. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's stage-in fetch.

column5: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: KernelStageIn, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column6: The runtime refuses a kernel's `[[stage_in]]` fetch of INLINE BYTES bound with `MTLAttributeStrideStatic`, where plain Metal answers. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording: `setBytes:length:attributeStride:atIndex:` of the source bytes with the constant, under a dynamic-stride layout, answered `0x110` and then `0x100` seven times -- the element at the bind offset for the first element and zero past it -- and the command buffer completed. Ours refuses at the dispatch, `Unsupported(KernelStageIn)`, from the bind state; `ComputeCommandEncoder::set_bytes_with_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/compute.rs:607) documents exactly that refusal and exactly that measured Metal answer, saying the fetch does not emulate it. By the owner's standing rule that what Metal allows we must allow, the refusal is a gap and not a settled difference. It is the same gap as the three `attribute-stride-*` divergences beside it and has the same fix -- teach `PushField::StageInStride` to say "the constant was bound" apart from "stride 0" and have the pulled read in crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs select the first element and zeros past it -- after which this refusal can be dropped. The buffer forms answer the wrong value instead of refusing, which is the worse half of the same bug; this form at least fails visibly. Scoped to every venue because the refusal is in the encoder's bind state, before any Vulkan call. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's stage-in fetch.

Metal's `half` result of a 16-bit float texel hands back the texel's own NaN code, with its sign, its payload and its signalling bit kept, and ours answers the one positive quiet NaN `0x7e00` for every one of them. Verified on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording of plain Metal read against our own codes at every one of the differing words of this run: Metal answers the twelve NaN codes of the case's own `V` table other than `0x7e00` -- `0x7c01`, `0x7d55`, `0x7dff`, `0x7e01`, `0x7f00`, `0x7fff`, `0xfc01`, `0xfdff`, `0xfe00`, `0xfe01`, `0xff00` and `0xffff` -- at 43 texels each and 42 for `0xff00`, which is 515, and ours answers `0x7e00` at all 1,545 differing words of the three sites without exception. No finite, zero, denormal or infinite texel differs anywhere, and the count is the same at all three access sites. Metal's stored blend result rounds the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carries the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)`, one fused multiply-add on the destination term -- and ours is the mirror image, `round(Sf*S + round(Df*D))`, the destination product rounded and the source product fused. Verified by measurement rather than from the notice: this case's own committed recording of plain Metal on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) and our own codes at every differing word of this run, both read against the case's own source sweep and destination generator, which a host with no Metal rebuilds. Metal's rule holds at 5,376 of 5,376 words over the eight divergent sites of the five divergent formats and ours at 5,376 of 5,376, with the 512 alpha words of the two `da-1mda` sites held out: there the source factor and the destination value are both the destination alpha, neither rule fits either side, and those 512 words are identical on the two sides, so they contribute no divergence (the differing words of `da-1mda` are the three colour channels alone). `half-output-blends-r32f`'s `sc-dc` is the control: there Metal rounds the destination product exactly as we do, at all 256 words of it. That case is not exact overall -- its `bc-1msa` site diverges once the blend-colour rows are compared -- so the control is that one site and not the case. So the gap is not half-precision rounding -- it is which of the two products the arithmetic keeps unrounded, which is why the two 32-bit float formats diverge too, and why `sc-dc`, whose source product `S*S` is exact in the attachment, still moves by a single code. Metal's rule is its compiler's fast-math fold of the attachment's blend and conversion into the fragment function, `rt6_samples` being a fast-math module; ours is the device's fixed-function blend, which the pipeline leaves the blend to and records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for (`pipeline/color_writes.rs`, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in `pipeline/stage_io.rs`). The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` at the attachment's own precision for a fast-math `half` colour output that reaches a blended attachment; that needs the destination value inside the shader and moves every such pipeline's module, so it is not this packet's. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in `pipeline/artifact.rs` says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the rows stay divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes are this venue's blend unit, which is why the rows name this venue. Open: translator and pipeline work, on the orchestrator's todo list.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: Some(\"MTLPixelFormatASTC_4x2_sRGB\") }"))
column6: The runtime holds no image of ASTC's 4x2 and 8x4 footprints, so `heapTextureSizeAndAlignWithDescriptor:` -- CPU arithmetic over a descriptor, which Metal answers for every one of them -- is refused `Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented)` out of the translator's format table (crates/metal2vulkan/src/metal/format/mod.rs, the `formats_named_not_held!` and `astc_without_a_vulkan_block!` patterns, whose `repr` is `NotImplemented`). Measured on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, in a throwaway process forked per (format, texture type): Metal answers a size and an alignment for every descriptor of this case, makes a texture of every format in every texture type bar the ones the case's own module records, and takes a host round trip through each. The whole of Metal's answer is in this case's recording, which is what an implementation will be held to. The case STOPS at this first refusal by design: the runtime refuses all 33 formats of the family, so recording a refusal per site and going on would print some 2900 `Refused` rows and need a ledger row for each. So this one row stands for the family, and the open work -- which formats, and what Metal answers for each -- is on the orchestrator's todo list with the measurements. Scoped `*` and not to a venue: the refusal is decided by the format table before any device is consulted, so no device can change it; verified on MoltenVK over this M3 Max (2026-10-24), unverified elsewhere by execution.

column1: # The texture-buffer creator's memoryless gap: plain Metal makes a `Memoryless` texture buffer
# (its `storageMode` 3 on an M3 Max) and `new_buffer` refuses the mode, which no Vulkan buffer
# has. The heap size query's memoryless gap is closed -- it answers Metal's uncompressed model
# (`texture/heap.rs`'s `memoryless_answer`) -- so only the creator's rows are left.

column6: Plain Metal makes a MTLStorageModeMemoryless TEXTURE BUFFER and the runtime refuses it `Invalid(StorageMode)` out of `new_buffer`, so the one texture type whose texels are a buffer's bytes is the one type whose memoryless form we have not got. Measured on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, a throwaway forked process: a TextureBuffer descriptor of 64 RGBA8Unorm texels, usage RenderTarget or ShaderRead, storage Memoryless answers a heap footprint of 256 bytes at an alignment of 16 - the same two numbers every other storage mode answers for that descriptor, so the mode changes nothing about a texture buffer's layout - and `newTextureWithDescriptor:` answers a texture whose storageMode is 3, mipmapLevelCount is its descriptor's and usage is echoed back. A distinct gap from the heap size query's memoryless gap, which is closed -- the query answers Metal's uncompressed model (`texture/heap.rs`'s `memoryless_answer`): this one is the CREATOR refusing, and it refuses deeper - a texture buffer is made over a buffer (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/buffer.rs, the `StorageMode::Memoryless => Err(invalid(call, Problem::StorageMode))` arm), and a memoryless buffer is a thing the runtime has no backing for at all, where Vulkan's nearest form is a lazily allocated allocation that the texture path already uses for a memoryless attachment (`texture/attachment_stand_in.rs`). So the fix is not the size query's: it is a memoryless backing for the buffer a texture buffer lies over, or a texture-buffer creator that does not go through `new_buffer` for this mode. Nothing in this tree says what a memoryless texture buffer's texels do - they cannot be read by the host and no pass targets a texture buffer - so what a fix owes beyond making the object and answering its getters is itself unmeasured, and measuring it is part of the work. Scoped to every venue: the refusal is in the runtime's own creator, before any device call. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Metal's `texture2d<half>` never widens, so a 16-bit float texel's NaN comes back as its own bits (verified: this case's own recording of plain Metal on an M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1). Ours reads the image as `f32` lanes and rounds them (`lower::texture::metal_texel_nans` keeps the device's decode for a half-channel class, which is exact only on a device that widens a half texel exactly), and this device's **sampler** canonicalizes a 16-bit float texel's NaN to 0xFFC00000, its own negative quiet NaN, so every NaN lane of a nearest sample reads 0xFE00 where Metal reads the texel's code. Its image **loads** keep the texel's bits, so `case/words/read` and `case/words/read-through-sample` are exact here, where all three sites differ on MoltenVK. The runtime announces `device-nan-encoding` for it. Open: read a 16-bit float texture's `half` result through an unsigned-integer alias of the image, the read side of the `StorageImageClass::HalfBits` write path, so no device decode sees the texel; on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal rasterizes a line by the diamond-exit rule and this driver's Bresenham mode breaks one tie the other way. The line of vertices 0 and 1 runs exactly through the boundary point (3.5, 1.0), a vertex of the diamonds of both pixels either side of it: Metal draws the lower pixel (row 1 column 3) and leaves row 0 column 3 at the pass's clear, and this driver draws row 0 column 3 and leaves row 1 column 3. Those two texels, and nothing else, are the whole of each cell's difference -- the mark word alone, since the fragment's vertex id is 0 either way. Vulkan's Bresenham diamond is the open set |p - x| + |q - y| < 0.5, so a line that only touches a vertex exits no diamond and the specification requires no fragment for either pixel; both choices conform, and llvmpipe (LLVM 23.1.1, Mesa 26.2.4) makes Metal's. The runtime already asks every line-rasterizing pipeline for VK_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_BRESENHAM_EXT (`pipeline/graphics.rs`), which is what took these four cells from 7, 7, 5 and 13 texels to these two: without it a strictLines device covers the whole rectangle of the line's width. There is no Vulkan control over the tie, so this is the driver's own and not the runtime's. RADV and ANV unrun. docs/FAST-PATHS.md carries the gap.

Those two texels, and nothing else, are the whole of each cell's difference -- the mark word alone, since the fragment's vertex id is 0 either way. Vulkan's Bresenham diamond is the open set |p - x| + |q - y| < 0.5, so a line that only touches a vertex exits no diamond and the specification requires no fragment for either pixel; both choices conform, and llvmpipe (LLVM 23.1.1, Mesa 26.2.4) makes Metal's. The runtime already asks every line-rasterizing pipeline for VK_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_BRESENHAM_EXT (`pipeline/graphics.rs`), which is what took these four cells from 7, 7, 5 and 13 texels to these two: without it a strictLines device covers the whole rectangle of the line's width. There is no Vulkan control over the tie, so this is the driver's own and not the runtime's. RADV and ANV unrun. docs/FAST-PATHS.md carries the gap.

Plain Metal makes a MTLStorageModeMemoryless TEXTURE BUFFER and the runtime refuses it `Invalid(StorageMode)` out of `new_buffer`, so the one texture type whose texels are a buffer's bytes is the one type whose memoryless form we have not got. What Metal does was measured on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, a throwaway forked process: a TextureBuffer descriptor of 64 RGBA8Unorm texels, usage RenderTarget or ShaderRead, storage Memoryless answers a heap footprint of 256 bytes at an alignment of 16 -- the same two numbers every other storage mode answers for that descriptor -- and `newTextureWithDescriptor:` answers a texture whose storageMode is 3. This is a distinct gap from the heap size query's memoryless gap, which is closed -- the query answers Metal's uncompressed model (`texture/heap.rs`'s `memoryless_answer`): the CREATOR refuses, and deeper -- a texture buffer is made over a buffer, and the `StorageMode::Memoryless => Err(invalid(call, Problem::StorageMode))` arm in crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/buffer.rs has no memoryless backing to give it, where Vulkan's nearest form is the lazily allocated allocation the texture path already uses for a memoryless attachment (`texture/attachment_stand_in.rs`). So the fix is not the size query's: it is a memoryless backing for the buffer a texture buffer lies over, or a texture-buffer creator that does not go through `new_buffer` for this mode. What a memoryless texture buffer's texels do is itself unmeasured -- the host cannot read them and no pass targets a texture buffer -- and measuring it is part of the work. The refusal is in the runtime's own creator before any device call, and this row records it on this venue, which is where this run measured it. Open: runtime work on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal's alpha-to-coverage covers `floor(alpha * rasterSampleCount)` samples, so at ONE sample an alpha of 0.5 covers NO sample and the destination survives the draw untouched; we store the fragment instead. Metal's rule is measured, and the one-sample row is what pins `floor` against round-to-nearest: this case's own committed recording, taken on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, holds the destination at every channel (the first differing element is Metal 255 against our 64, the fragment's own 0.25 channel as a code), and the four elements of the site are the one texel's four channels with a bound of 191. So this is not a rounding of any kind: a whole fragment is stored where Metal stores nothing. The cause is that we hand the field to the device as `VkPipelineMultisampleStateCreateInfo::alphaToCoverageEnable` and Vulkan leaves the alpha-to-coverage mapping implementation-defined, so the device rounds where Metal floors, and at one sample the two rules disagree about the whole pixel. The exact form is ours to compute: derive the coverage from the output alpha in the fragment function by Metal's floor rule and write it as the sample mask, ANDed with a mask the fragment already writes (which this family measured Metal to AND, and which a device-computed coverage cannot honour in that order), rather than enabling the device's field. That is translator and pipeline work and it changes every alpha-to-coverage pipeline's module. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal's stored code and ours differ by one at this site, in a draw whose blend reads the source alpha with `alphaToOneEnabled` set and clear. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Alpha-to-one itself is exact here -- the field's own cell, the stored colour moving from the source blended at 0.5 to the source alone, holds on both legs -- so what is left is the one-code rounding of the blend, and the `-off-` leg diverging too is what says the alpha-to-one field is not in it. Our side gives Metal's codes there, so the blend colour is not the disagreement. The disagreement is the product rounding this family's other rows describe -- Metal `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)`, ours `round(Sf*S + round(Df*D))` -- and the honest limit of this row is that the rule has NOT been shown to fit these sites: `bc-1msa` departs from it at the first word of `r16f` (Metal stores 0.60498046875 where the rule gives 0.6044921875), so `MEASURED` in that module still names only the eight sites the rule was measured over and no rule is asserted here. The fix is the same fix: fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does for a fast-math `half` colour output reaching a blended attachment, which needs the destination value inside the shader. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'. Metal's `half` result of a 16-bit float texel hands back the texel's own NaN code, with its sign, its payload and its signalling bit kept (verified: this case's own committed recording of plain Metal on an M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1), and ours answers a canonicalized code. The cause is that our `half` texel access reads the image as `f32` lanes and converts them back: `lower/texture/half.rs` takes the image instruction's `f32` texel through `narrow::round_texel`, so whatever the device's half-to-float decode canonicalizes is already gone before our conversion sees it. On this venue 215 words a channel differ at EACH of the three access sites with a bound of 512, which is a narrower loss than the Apple venue's (515 words at a bound of 33279, the sign bit among them) and a wider reach than RADV's (where the image loads keep the bits and only the nearest sample moves): this device's decode keeps the sign of every NaN and some of the payload, and all three access paths lose the rest. Exactly which codes survive here is NOT established by this run -- it was read off the report's per-site counts and bound, not off a word-by-word comparison, and a word-by-word read of this venue's own transcript is the first step. The exact form is the one the other venues' rows name: read a half-float texture through its 16-bit integer alias and assemble the `half` from its bits, the read side of the `StorageImageClass::HalfBits` aliasing the translator already has for half texel writes (`lower/texture/slice.rs`), which changes the slot's view and costs per-access work, so by the owner's fast-default rule it belongs behind a `DevicePolicy` switch with its docs/FAST-PATHS.md row. Announced as `device-nan-encoding`, whose own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so the row stays divergent. This is NOT a rounding difference and it is not the narrow-float NaN gap of the sibling rows in the same case. Metal's `float4` fetch of an `MTLVertexFormatFloatRGB9E5` attribute answers 1.0 (0x3F800000) in the fourth component, the missing-component default of a three-channel format, and we answer 0 (0x0) -- the first differing element of every one of these sites. Beyond the default, the `float4` and `half4` legs move 38 of the site's elements with a bound of 65409, a whole value at the top of the format's range (its largest representable value is 65408), so this device's decode of the shared 5-bit exponent parts from Metal's as well, where the `instance-step` leg's 12 differing elements all move by exactly 1 and are consistent with the fourth-component default alone. Metal's compute pipeline state answers `staticThreadgroupMemoryLength` 24576 -- the fixture's own 24 KiB `threadgroup` array -- and we answer 32768 on this venue. This getter is the one the case compares precisely because it is the SHADER's own number and so the same wherever the shader is compiled, which this case's module docs state outright, so unlike the threadgroup-size facts beside it this is not a device limit: it is a number of ours that is not Metal's. The cause is deliberate and is in one place: on a device that emulates simdgroups the reported length is `fixed + ceil(max/32) * per_simdgroup` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/compile/api.rs, the `static_bytes` match), which folds the emulated simdgroup scratch into the public getter so that, as the comment there says, any `[[threadgroup(n)]]` lengths that fit beside the reported length fit every threadgroup up to the maximum. The fix is to unfold the two uses: answer the kernel's own `static_threadgroup_bytes` from the getter and keep the scratch in the planner's budget, which already carries it as `RuntimeFact::SimdgroupEmulation{bytes_per_simdgroup, arena}` and already refuses a kernel whose arena and one simdgroup's scratch exceed `maxComputeSharedMemorySize` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/simd/workgroup.rs's `check`). What that costs is that a dispatch whose dynamic lengths fit beside Metal's 24576 but not beside the real 32768 must be refused or re-planned rather than silently prevented by an inflated getter, and whether every such dispatch is reachable through the planner's existing check is NOT established here. Metal DROPS what a shader or the blit engine writes into memory whose backing is read-only, silently and with no error, and we land the write. Metal's rule is measured, not assumed: `probes/readonly_gpu_writes.m` ran eleven shapes on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, one shape a process, eight runs a shape, each against a writable twin of the same program, and a kernel's stores and a pass's visibility result both complete with no error while neither a later command buffer nor the CPU sees any of it -- the writable twin landing its write in all three places is what makes 'dropped' a measurement. The two read-only states agree: bit 24 of `MTLResourceOptions` (what this case states, `ResourceOptions::PRIVATE_BIT`) and the production SPI pair `detachBacking` plus `replaceBackingWithRanges:readOnly:YES` answer alike on all ten shapes measurable under both. The owner's standing rule is that where Metal drops such a write we drop it too, on EVERY driver, with no refusal. We do it on macOS alone: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/read_only_view.rs imports the pages through a read-only view of them (`mach_vm_remap` then `mprotect`), and `VIEWS_DROP_WRITES` is `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`, so on a Linux driver the import is of the caller's own pages, the GPU's writes reach them, and the difference is announced as `Degradation::PrivateResourceOption`. The announcement is not a justification here: the case declares nothing of it and the bytes differ. What the exact form is on a Linux driver is NOT established -- the module's own measurement is that those drivers pin imported pages for writing and refuse or fault on read-only ones (`host_memory.rs`), so the read-only-view trick does not carry over -- and finding one is the work this row waits on. Metal's `MTLStoreActionDontCare` leaves the attachment holding the texels it held BEFORE the pass, and we leave what the pass rendered. Metal's answer is this case's own committed recording on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1 and it is sharper than a guess would be: under `DontCare` then `MTLLoadActionLoad` pass A's clear AND its draw are both gone and the host's per-texel write survives in pass A's own region. The four cells of this case that diverge here are exactly the `MTLStoreActionDontCare` ones, and the eight that do not are untouched, so the sequence, the render-area bounds and both load actions are right -- it is the store alone. The cause is deliberate and documented: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/render_target.rs hands Vulkan `DONT_CARE` only on a driver measured to keep one of Metal's two answers (`DriverFact::DontCareStoreIsMetals` or `DontCareStoreIsOneOfMetals`, MoltenVK on the M4 and the M3 Max) and stores the attachment (`STORE`) on every other, because Vulkan leaves a `DONT_CARE` attachment's contents undefined and a driver may answer a third thing neither of Metal's -- the module records NVIDIA's leaving a pass's clear under its draw. `STORE` is Metal's OTHER answer, the one its tiler gives on overflow, so it is a recorded near-equivalent and the runtime announces `dont-care-store` for it; but it is not the answer this case's Metal recording holds, and a program that reads such an attachment after the pass sees pass A's result here where Metal gives it the prior texels. The exact form is to restore those texels rather than pick one of Metal's answers: keep them and put them back around the pass, the shape `kept_bytes.rs` already uses for a texture over a buffer, which costs a copy per `DontCare` attachment -- so by the owner's fast-default rule it belongs behind a `DevicePolicy` switch with its docs/FAST-PATHS.md row and `STORE` stays the default. Open: runtime work, on the orchestrator's todo list.

column6: Metal resolves a multisampled depth/stencil attachment with the stencil filter `MTLMultisampleStencilResolveFilterSample0` under the depth filter `Min` or `Max`, and we refuse it `NotImplemented(DepthStencilResolve)`. Ours is not a device refusal dressed up: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/resolve.rs states in its own words that a filter the device's resolve modes lack -- `supportedDepthResolveModes`, `supportedStencilResolveModes`, or the other aspect's modes where a subpass resolving one aspect must name the same mode for both, read off the compile device's description as `VkProperty::{DepthResolveMode, StencilResolveMode, IndependentResolveNone, IndependentResolve}` -- is 'not built', and names the exact path in the same sentence: a resolve DRAW, which the module already uses for other unresolvable pairs and which needs no resolve mode from the device at all. So the gap is work not done rather than a capability missing, which is what makes it ours under the owner's rule that what Metal allows we must allow. This venue is a device with no independent resolve of the two aspects, so the `Sample0` stencil filter cannot be named beside a `Min` or `Max` depth one; the case's other filter pairs run here, so it is these two cells. The fix belongs in resolve.rs: reach the resolve draw for a filter pair the device's modes cannot state, as the module does where `DepthResolvedSample` follows `Min` or `Max` on a sampled attachment. Metal's tile render pipeline state answers `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` 1024 and ours answers 960 on this venue. The 960 is this device's own compiled limit and the runtime reports it deliberately: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/tile.rs documents the answer as 'Metal's 1024, or the descriptor's limit, where the device runs a threadgroup of 1024 threads, else the device's lower limit', and lavapipe's emulated 32-lane simdgroups take 960 threads of this pipeline. So the number is honest about the device and a dispatch past it is refused typed -- which this family's own test `a_dispatch_the_device_cannot_take_is_the_devices_gap` rules is the DEVICE's gap and verdicts `LacksFeature`. The open work is that the same ruling has not reached the FACT: the state's reported limit is compared against Metal's number as if it were an answer of ours, so a venue whose threadgroup is smaller reads as a divergence at the getter while the matching dispatch reads as the venue's honest gap. That inconsistency is the suite's, which is ours, and the fix is in crates/metal2vulkan-conformance: let a state fact that reports a device limit follow the device-gap ruling its dispatch already gets, or state Metal's number beside the device's so the comparison asks the right question. Until it does the row records it, and the row must not be read as a claim that the runtime should report 1024 on a device that cannot run it: that would be a lie a consumer sizes a dispatch from. Open: suite work, on the orchestrator's todo list.
